use_cases.name: Ingest punches from every enrolled source
use_cases.goal: Capture every attendance punch from any enrolled source exactly once, store it immutably and queue the affected attendance day for derivation.

stakeholders.interest: Every punch reaches the platform, including those taken while a terminal or phone was offline, so daily attendance needs no manual reconstruction.
Locked payroll inputs are never changed silently by a punch that arrives late.
Raw punches and any clock corrections are retained side by side and can be traced to the device that produced them.

use_cases.trigger: A worker punches at a biometric terminal, kiosk, geofenced mobile app, business messaging channel, web page or integrated gate system.
preconditions: The worker holds an active assignment and is enrolled on the source used to punch.
The terminal or kiosk is registered to a location and has completed at least one clock sync with the platform.
The set of enabled punch sources is configured for the tenant (RL-070).
postconditions_success: One immutable attendance_event exists with person, punch time, direction, source and device, and time.punch.received and time.punch.ingested have been emitted.
Repeat punches inside the 60-second dedupe window are stored and marked as duplicates rather than dropped.
The affected attendance date is in the recompute queue (attendance_day state PENDING) and time.recompute.requested has been emitted.
postconditions_failure: A punch for a date inside a locked payroll period is stored and raised as an exception; the locked attendance day is unchanged.
A punch held offline beyond the 7-day queue limit is not replayed and must be recovered through regularisation (TIM-08).

main_flow.action: Punches IN or OUT at an enrolled source, which captures person, time, direction, device and, on mobile, location and selfie reference.
Pushes the punch batch to the ingestion endpoint, or the site agent polls the device buffer and pushes it; received_at is stamped.
De-duplicates on person, punch time and device within the 60-second window and stores the raw event immutably.
Queues the person's affected attendance date for derivation with reason new_punch and emits time.recompute.requested.

alternate_flows.condition: The terminal, kiosk or phone has no connection to the platform when the worker punches.
steps: The source queues the punch locally with a signed timestamp.
On reconnect the source replays queued punches in order, keeping the original punch time and adding the actual received_at.

alternate_flows.condition: The terminal clock has drifted from platform time.
steps: The platform corrects punch time using the device's last sync offset, within the configured maximum of plus or minus 120,000 ms.
The correction is recorded and the raw device value is retained beside it.

alternate_flows.condition: The worker punches through the business messaging channel instead of a terminal or app.
steps: The channel relays the punch with the worker's verified identity and message timestamp to the same ingestion service.

exception_flows.condition: A second punch from the same person and device arrives inside the 60-second dedupe window.
exception_flows.handling: The event is stored with is_duplicate set, excluded from pairing and counted towards the device health signal; it is never discarded.

exception_flows.condition: The punch belongs to a date inside a locked payroll period.
exception_flows.handling: The attendance day is not re-queued; an attendance exception is raised for time office and payroll review instead of changing the locked day.

exception_flows.condition: A locally queued punch is older than the 7-day queue limit when connectivity returns.
exception_flows.handling: The punch is not replayed automatically; the worker or supervisor recovers the time through a regularisation in the exception queue.

nfrs: Sustains a peak of 500 punches per second per tenant without loss or reordering of a person's events.
Offline sources retain queued punches with signed timestamps for at least 7 days.
Raw attendance events are append-only; corrections are stored as additional values, never as overwrites.

use_cases.name: Derive the attendance day from paired punches
use_cases.goal: Turn a person's punches into one attendance day keyed on the shift start date, with segments, breaks, gross, net and raw overtime, stamped with provenance.

stakeholders.interest: A night that runs past midnight counts as one working day and the next day is not marked absent.
Breaks such as the dinner gap are reportable on their own without a special query.
Gross, net and overtime figures follow the client's configured break and overtime basis, so pay inputs are correct.
Every computed day carries the ruleset version and every recomputation leaves a field-level delta.

use_cases.trigger: A punch lands for the day (TIM-01) or a recompute is requested for it (TIM-09).
preconditions: The attendance date is queued for derivation (attendance_day state PENDING).
The applied shift and the tenant's break-deduction and overtime-basis settings are effective for the date.
Gate passes for the date, if any, are recorded with their approval status.
postconditions_success: attendance_day is COMPUTED with first_in, last_out, gross, recorded and deducted break minutes, net minutes and ot_minutes_raw.
One attendance_segment exists per IN/OUT pair and one attendance_break per gap between segments.
computed_at, ruleset version and input hash are stamped and time.attendance_day.computed is emitted; a recompute that changed values has written attendance_day_delta rows.
postconditions_failure: Where an event cannot be paired, the day is in EXCEPTION state, the event is retained and an exception is raised to the queue (TIM-08).

main_flow.action: Sets attendance_date to the date the shift started, so a shift that runs past midnight stays on one day.
Collects all of the person's events inside the 30-hour day window and orders them by timestamp.
Pairs each IN with the next OUT and writes one attendance_segment per pair.
Writes each gap between consecutive segments as an attendance_break with a break type (meal, gate_pass, other) and a paid flag.
Computes gross_minutes as last OUT minus first IN.
Computes recorded and deducted break minutes and net_minutes per the tenant's break treatment; the demo client records breaks without deducting them.
Deducts gate-pass gaps as breaks and credits back the minutes of approved gate passes before disposition.
Computes ot_minutes_raw as the greater of zero and basis minus shift minutes, using gross or net as configured (gross for the demo client).
Stamps computed_at, ruleset version and input hash, and emits time.attendance_day.computed.
When recomputing an existing day, writes an attendance_day_delta per changed field instead of overwriting silently.

alternate_flows.condition: The tenant is configured to deduct recorded breaks from net time.
steps: Break minutes are written as both recorded and deducted.
net_minutes is gross minus deducted breaks, so a 19h20m span with a 45-minute break gives 18h35m.

alternate_flows.condition: The tenant's overtime basis is net rather than gross.
steps: ot_minutes_raw is computed from net_minutes against shift minutes.

alternate_flows.condition: The recomputed day is identical to the stored day.
steps: The stored row is left as it is and no delta or recomputed event is written.

exception_flows.condition: An IN has no following OUT, or an OUT has no preceding IN, inside the day window.
exception_flows.handling: No segment is written for the event, the event is retained, the day enters EXCEPTION state and an unpaired-punch exception is raised to the queue.

exception_flows.condition: A gate-pass gap exists but the pass is pending or rejected.
exception_flows.handling: The gap stays deducted as a gate_pass break and no minutes are credited until approval triggers a recompute.

nfrs: Derivation is deterministic: identical inputs and ruleset version always produce an identical attendance_day row (property TC-PR06).
For every day, segment minutes plus break minutes equal gross minutes (property TC-PR07).
Break treatment and overtime basis are tenant configuration; changing them requires no release.

user_stories.want: a shift that runs past midnight to be one attendance day on the date it started
user_stories.so_that: night workers are neither split across two days nor marked absent the next morning

use_cases.name: Infer the applied shift from the first in-punch
use_cases.goal: Apply the shift a worker actually punched into, record it against the rostered shift and let the roster owner correct it.

stakeholders.interest: Sees when actual coverage departed from the published roster.
Is judged against the thresholds of the shift actually worked, not the one rostered.
Every override of an inferred shift names who changed it and why.

use_cases.trigger: The first in-punch of a person's day is derived.
preconditions: A published roster or an assignment default shift exists for the date.
Each shift in the shift group has a non-overlapping inference window (earliest_in, latest_in).
postconditions_success: attendance_day records shift_id_assigned and shift_id_applied, and the inference reason where they differ.
time.shift.inferred (and time.shift.overridden after a correction) has been emitted.
Disposition thresholds are looked up using the applied shift's duration.
postconditions_failure: Where no inference window matches, the assigned shift is applied and an exception is raised for review.

main_flow.action: Reads the assigned shift for the date from the published roster, falling back to the assignment default.
Checks whether the first in-punch falls inside another shift's inference window within the same shift group.
Adopts the inferred shift for the day, records assigned shift, applied shift and inference reason, and emits time.shift.inferred.
Reviews the inferred shift on the attendance day detail and overrides it, with a reason, where the inference is wrong.
Passes the applied shift's duration to the disposition threshold lookup (TIM-05).

alternate_flows.condition: The first in-punch falls inside the assigned shift's own window.
steps: The assigned shift is recorded as the applied shift and no inference event is emitted.

alternate_flows.condition: The roster owner agrees with the inferred shift.
steps: No override is recorded and the inferred shift stands.

exception_flows.condition: While configuring the shift group, a window is saved that overlaps another shift's window in the same group.
exception_flows.handling: The save fails validation and names both shifts and the overlapping interval; no ambiguous inference can occur at run time.

exception_flows.condition: The first in-punch falls outside every inference window in the group.
exception_flows.handling: The assigned shift is applied and an inferred-shift exception is raised to the attendance exception queue for review.

exception_flows.condition: An override is submitted without a reason.
exception_flows.handling: The override is rejected; actor and reason are mandatory for the audit entry.

nfrs: Inference is never silent: every day where applied differs from assigned is visible to the roster owner on the attendance day detail.
Inference windows are configuration rows validated at save time.

user_stories.want: the shift to be taken from the time a worker actually punched in
user_stories.so_that: a worker who covers B shift is processed on B shift without me editing the roster

acceptance.given: an employee rostered to shift A (08:00-20:00) whose first in-punch is 20:05, inside shift B's window
acceptance.then: shift applied is B, shift assigned remains A, the inference reason is recorded and time.shift.inferred is emitted

user_stories.so_that: the day is judged on the correct shift and the change is auditable

use_cases.name: Resolve the day type before disposition
use_cases.goal: Decide whether each attendance day is a working day, weekly off, holiday or festival for that worker, from the location calendar and the worker's class, before any threshold is applied.

stakeholders.interest: Working on a rest day is never mistaken for a short working day.
Policy follows the worker class, so two classes under one contractor are treated correctly.
Rest-day and holiday working feed overtime eligibility correctly (TIM-07).

use_cases.trigger: An attendance day reaches the point before disposition.
preconditions: A work calendar and holiday calendar are published for the worker's location and year.
The worker's assignment carries a worker class effective on the date, with has_rest_days and rest_day_pattern set.
postconditions_success: attendance_day.day_type is written before any disposition threshold is applied.
Workers of different classes at the same vendor, site and shift carry day types from their own class policy.
postconditions_failure: Where the calendar or class cannot be resolved, the day is not disposed and a missing-data exception is raised.

main_flow.action: Resolves the day type for the location and date from its work and holiday calendars: working, weekly off, holiday or festival.
Overlays the worker class's rest-day policy (has_rest_days, rest_day_pattern) as effective on that date.
Where workers share vendor, site and shift but differ in class, resolves each worker by their own class policy.
Writes day_type on the attendance day before disposition thresholds are applied.

alternate_flows.condition: The worker's class has no rest days, as for daily-wage contractual workers.
steps: A calendar weekly off such as Sunday resolves to Working for this worker.

alternate_flows.condition: All workers in the vendor, site and shift group belong to the same class.
steps: The single class policy is applied to every worker in the group.

exception_flows.condition: Disposition is requested for a day whose day_type has not yet been written.
exception_flows.handling: Disposition is refused and the day is re-queued so that day type resolves first; a rest-day volunteer can never be marked Half Day.

exception_flows.condition: No published calendar exists for the worker's location and date.
exception_flows.handling: The day is held undisposed and a missing-data exception is raised to the attendance exception queue for the time office.

nfrs: Calendars are held per location, so plants in different states never share one holiday list.
Rest-day policy is read as effective on the attendance date, not as at today.

user_stories.want: daily-wage contractual workers with no rest days to show Sunday as a working day
user_stories.so_that: their attendance and daily wages are computed on the days they are expected to work

user_stories.so_that: employees and helpers supplied by the same vendor each get their own entitlement

use_cases.name: Dispose the attendance day against shift thresholds and late rules
use_cases.goal: Assign Present, Half Day, Absent or a non-working status to each day using thresholds for the applied shift's length, grace, the monthly late allowance, designation exemption and long-night relief, with the rule trail stored.

stakeholders.interest: Sees the late counter and the rules behind every status, so penalties are never silent.
Can defend any disputed status from its stored rule trail.
Half-day and absent statuses that drive loss-of-pay are correct before the payroll cut-off.

use_cases.trigger: Totals for the attendance day have been computed (TIM-02) and the day type resolved (TIM-04).
preconditions: attendance_day holds net (or configured basis) minutes, the applied shift and day_type.
attendance_rule_set has a threshold row for the applied shift's duration (12h, 10h, 9h or 8h for the demo client).
The employee's designation band carries the grace_exempt attribute.
postconditions_success: attendance_day.status is written with applied_rule_ids and time.attendance_day.disposed is emitted.
late_by_minutes and the monthly late counter are updated and visible to the employee (time.late.counted).
postconditions_failure: Where no threshold row exists for the applied shift duration, the day is left undisposed and an exception is raised for configuration.

main_flow.action: Checks whether the day type is anything other than Working.
Looks up absent, half-day and grace thresholds for the applied shift's duration from attendance_rule_set.
Checks whether net (or configured basis) minutes fall below the absent threshold, for example 6:30 on a 12-hour shift.
Checks whether they fall below the half-day threshold, for example 11:30 on a 12-hour shift.
Computes late_by_minutes against shift start plus 15 minutes of grace, with grace applied to both the in and the out punch.
Checks whether the employee's designation band is grace-exempt (Assistant Manager and above for the demo client).
Increments the monthly late-instance counter, visible to the employee; three instances per calendar month are forgiven.
Checks whether this is the fourth or later late instance in the calendar month.
Checks whether the previous attendance day ended after the long-night hour (03:00), allowing arrival up to 09:30.
Writes the status with the IDs of the rules that produced it and emits time.attendance_day.disposed.

alternate_flows.condition: The day type is weekly off, holiday or festival.
steps: Status is set to the day type, or to 'day type - worked' where punches exist.
Thresholds and late rules are skipped and the day passes to overtime eligibility (TIM-07).

alternate_flows.condition: Basis minutes are below the absent threshold (390/360/300/270 for 12h/10h/9h/8h shifts).
steps: Status is set to Absent with RL-112 recorded.

alternate_flows.condition: Basis minutes are below the half-day threshold (690/570/510/450 for 12h/10h/9h/8h shifts).
steps: Status is set to Half Day with RL-113 recorded.

alternate_flows.condition: The designation band is grace-exempt.
steps: No late instance is recorded and no late deduction applies.

alternate_flows.condition: The arrival is the fourth or later late instance this month.
steps: Status becomes Half Day even where hours qualify as Present, with RL-117 recorded.

alternate_flows.condition: The previous day's last OUT was after 03:00, today's arrival is no later than 09:30 and work continues until at least 20:00.
steps: The arrival is not treated as late, the late instance from step 7 is withdrawn and a full day is credited with RL-118 recorded.

exception_flows.condition: No threshold row exists for the applied shift's duration.
exception_flows.handling: The day is not disposed; an exception is raised so the implementation consultant adds the threshold row as configuration, then the day is recomputed.

exception_flows.condition: A working day has no punches at all.
exception_flows.handling: A no-punch exception is raised to the attendance exception queue and the day awaits regularisation or leave before final status.

nfrs: A new shift length is supported by adding a threshold row, with no release.
My attendance shows the last 60 days and the current late count even when the phone is offline.
Every status is explainable from its stored applied_rule_ids without re-running the rules.

user_stories.want: half-day and absent thresholds to follow the length of the shift applied
user_stories.so_that: workers on 8, 9, 10 and 12-hour shifts are judged against their own thresholds

acceptance.given: three working days on a 12-hour shift with net hours of 11:45, 11:00 and 6:00
acceptance.then: the statuses are Present, Half Day and Absent respectively

acceptance.given: E1041 on a 10-hour shift on 07 Sep with net hours of 9:15
acceptance.then: the status is Half Day because 9:15 is below 9:30, and RL-113 appears in the rule trail

user_stories.want: to see how many late arrivals I have used this month
user_stories.so_that: I know before a fourth late arrival turns a day into a half day

acceptance.when: she opens My attendance on 07 Sep

acceptance.when: she arrives at 09:25, as on each of her five late days in September

acceptance.given: a non-exempt colleague arrives at 09:25 on the same shift

user_stories.so_that: I am not penalised for staying until the early hours to finish the work

acceptance.when: he arrives at 09:25 on 09 Sep and leaves at 20:10

acceptance.then: the relief window does not apply and the arrival is counted as late against the 08:00 shift start

use_cases.name: Request, approve and credit a gate pass
use_cases.goal: Let an employee step out during a shift on an approved gate pass, enforce the personal monthly ceiling in the service and credit approved minutes back into work hours.

stakeholders.interest: Approves only passes that are within entitlement and sees the remaining allowance.
The ceiling is applied identically on every channel, so no pass slips through the messaging route.
Approved pass minutes do not reduce net hours; unapproved absence does.

use_cases.trigger: An employee requests a gate pass.
preconditions: The employee holds an active assignment with a gate-pass entitlement of 240 minutes and 2 personal instances per calendar month.
An approval chain for gate passes is defined for the employee's class and location (RL-010).
postconditions_success: gate_pass is approved, time.gate_pass.approved is emitted and the day is queued for recompute.
The approved minutes are credited back into work hours before disposition, so net hours are unchanged by the pass.
postconditions_failure: A personal pass that would breach the ceiling is rejected at validation with the ceiling named; nothing reaches the approver.
A rejected or pending pass credits nothing and the absence stays deducted.

main_flow.action: Requests a gate pass with date, from and to times, type (personal or official) and reason.
For a personal pass, checks whether it would exceed 240 minutes or 2 instances in the calendar month.
Approves or rejects the pass in the approvals inbox, on the chain resolved for the request type, class and location.
On approval, credits the approved minutes back into work hours before disposition thresholds and requests recompute of the day.
Tracks official passes on the employee's record without counting them against the personal ceiling.

alternate_flows.condition: The employee raises the request through the business messaging channel.
steps: The channel passes the request to the same gate-pass service, which applies the same validation as the web and app forms.

alternate_flows.condition: The pass type is official.
steps: The personal ceiling check is skipped and the pass is routed for approval.

alternate_flows.condition: The approver rejects the pass.
steps: The pass is closed as rejected with the approver's reason.
The time away stays deducted as a gate_pass break when the day is derived.

exception_flows.condition: The personal pass would take the month beyond 240 minutes or beyond 2 instances.
exception_flows.handling: The request is rejected at validation with reason text naming the ceiling and the amount already used; it is not routed to the approver.

exception_flows.condition: The day is derived while the pass is still pending.
exception_flows.handling: No minutes are credited; the gap stays deducted until approval triggers a recompute.

nfrs: The ceiling is enforced in the gate-pass service, so every channel returns the same decision for the same request.
Remaining personal minutes and instances for the month are shown to the employee before submission.

use_cases.name: Compute and approve overtime
use_cases.goal: Turn raw overtime minutes into an approved, payable overtime record that respects class eligibility, the state multiplier and the run in which it will be paid.

stakeholders.interest: Eligible overtime is recorded at the right rate and paid in the expected run.
Only approved overtime reaches the pay run, and overtime cannot be pulled into the salary run.
Approved overtime feeds the statutory overtime register and statutory limits are flagged before approval.

use_cases.trigger: An attendance day is computed with ot_minutes_raw greater than zero or is worked on a rest day or holiday.
preconditions: attendance_day is COMPUTED with ot_minutes_raw and day_type.
The person's ot_eligibility (always, rest_day_and_holiday_only or none) is resolved from class and assignment.
The state rule pack provides the overtime multiplier and weekly limit (2.0 multiplier for the demo client).
postconditions_success: overtime_record exists with minutes, eligibility basis, day type and multiplier, approved by the manager (time.overtime.approved).
The record is tagged with the run that will pay it; for the demo client this is the off-cycle run after salary.
postconditions_failure: Ineligible or rejected overtime has zero payable minutes; raw minutes are retained for reporting.

main_flow.action: Reads ot_minutes_raw from the attendance day and the person's resolved overtime eligibility.
Checks whether overtime eligibility is none.
Checks whether eligibility is rest-day-and-holiday-only and applies it against the resolved day type.
Writes the overtime_record with eligibility basis, day type and state rule-pack multiplier, and emits time.overtime.computed.
Reviews the overtime in the approvals inbox and approves it before it becomes payable.
Tags the approved overtime with the run that will pay it, regular or off-cycle (off-cycle after salary for the demo client).

alternate_flows.condition: Eligibility is none.
steps: Payable overtime is set to zero and the raw minutes are kept on the record for reporting.
No approval task is created.

alternate_flows.condition: Eligibility is rest-day-and-holiday-only.
steps: On a working day payable overtime is zero despite a span above shift length.
On a rest day or holiday the whole worked span is payable overtime.

alternate_flows.condition: The manager rejects the overtime.
steps: The record is marked rejected with the reason; payable minutes are zero and raw minutes remain for reporting.

exception_flows.condition: Approving the overtime would exceed the statutory weekly limit in the state rule pack (to be validated by Legal).
exception_flows.handling: The approver sees a warning naming the limit and the excess minutes; overtime is never paid past a limit silently.

exception_flows.condition: An overtime payment run is started before the linked salary run is closed.
exception_flows.handling: The run is blocked; after the salary run closes the overtime run executes and posts separately.

nfrs: Approved overtime records are retained long-term as the source for the statutory overtime register.
Overtime eligibility and multiplier are configuration (class and state rule pack), not code.

user_stories.so_that: only overtime I have checked becomes payable

use_cases.name: Resolve attendance exceptions through regularisation
use_cases.goal: Raise attendance exceptions, let the governed attendance agent propose evidence-based regularisations and have a manager or HR decide them so the day can be recomputed.

stakeholders.interest: A missed punch is corrected quickly from evidence, without a paper form.
The daily queue is triaged before it reaches people, with low-risk fixes handled within policy.
Every agent proposal and decision is in the action ledger with its evidence and simulation.

use_cases.trigger: An unpaired punch, missing punch on a working day, offline device, inferred shift, missing regularisation or late-threshold crossing is detected.
preconditions: The attendance day has been derived and the condition detected.
The tenant's auto-resolve threshold for the agent is configured (120 minutes illustrative).
postconditions_success: A regularisation is approved (time.regularisation.approved), the day is queued for recompute and the exception is closed.
Agent proposals and decisions are recorded in the action ledger.
postconditions_failure: A rejected proposal leaves the exception open with the rejection reason, and the attendance day stays in EXCEPTION state.

main_flow.action: Raises exceptions for unpaired punch, no punch on a working day, device offline, inferred shift, missing regularisation or late-threshold crossing.
Triages the queue and proposes a regularisation from device and roster evidence, with a dry-run diff and confidence, logged to the ledger.
Approves, amends or rejects the proposed regularisation, recording a reason.
Queues recompute for the affected day and closes the exception.

alternate_flows.condition: The proposed change is within the tenant's auto-resolve threshold and auto-resolve is enabled.
steps: The agent applies the regularisation under its scoped role and records it in the action ledger as auto-resolved.

alternate_flows.condition: The approver amends the proposal, for example a different OUT time.
steps: The approver edits the proposed values and sees a refreshed dry-run diff before approving.

alternate_flows.condition: No device or roster evidence supports a proposal.
steps: The agent leaves the exception unproposed and flags it for manual regularisation by the manager or time office.

exception_flows.condition: The proposed change exceeds the auto-resolve threshold.
exception_flows.handling: The agent may only propose; the change waits for a human decision.

exception_flows.condition: The approver rejects the proposal.
exception_flows.handling: The exception stays open with the rejection reason and the employee is asked for evidence or a leave request.

exception_flows.condition: The regularised date lies in a locked payroll period.
exception_flows.handling: The locked day is not changed; recompute raises an arrears item for the next open run.

nfrs: The agent acts only through declared tools under a role narrower than its human owner, and every action is ledgered.
Each proposal carries its evidence reference and dry-run result so an approver can decide without opening another screen.

user_stories.want: the agent to propose a fix for a missed punch with evidence and a preview of the result
user_stories.so_that: I can clear the exception queue in one decision per item

acceptance.given: E1026 Manjunath Poojary has an IN at 20:02 on 05 Sep with no matching OUT (exception EX-2026-0341), and the gate security register shows his exit at 08:12
acceptance.then: I see the register evidence, a dry-run diff setting last_out and gross minutes and adding a 12-minute overtime line, and a confidence value

acceptance.given: I approve the proposal
acceptance.then: a regularisation is created, recompute is queued for 05 Sep and EX-2026-0341 is closed

use_cases.name: Recompute attendance after a change
use_cases.goal: Re-derive every affected attendance day after a late punch, regularisation, rule change, roster republish or policy change, using inputs as at the snapshot and never altering a locked payroll period.

stakeholders.interest: Locked periods stay locked; corrections arrive as arrears in the next open run.
A policy change dated in the future does not rewrite the past.
Corrections reach attendance and pay without anyone re-entering data.

use_cases.trigger: A recompute request lands for a late punch, regularisation, rule change, roster republish, policy or class change, gate pass or leave reversal.
preconditions: The recompute queue holds person, date range and reason for each request.
Effective-dated history exists for worker class, assignment, shift, rule set and calendar.
postconditions_success: Every affected day in open periods is recomputed, deltas are written and time.attendance_day.recomputed is emitted.
Days in locked or closed payroll periods are unchanged and an arrears item exists for the next open run.
postconditions_failure: Days that still cannot be paired remain in EXCEPTION state in the exception queue.

main_flow.action: Consumes recompute queue entries of person, date range and reason, such as late punch, regularisation, rule change or roster republish.
Reads worker class, assignment, shift, rule set and calendar as at the recompute snapshot, never as at today.
Re-runs derivation, shift inference, day type and disposition for every affected day in an isolated worker process.
Checks whether any affected date falls inside a locked or closed payroll period.
Emits the delta set for audit and for the pre-payroll check on days not recomputed since the last rule change.

alternate_flows.condition: The reason is a change to class, rest days, shift group, grace exemption or location.
steps: The platform derives the affected population and date range from the change's effective date and queues them automatically.

alternate_flows.condition: A recomputed day is identical to the stored day.
steps: No delta is written for that day.

exception_flows.condition: An affected date lies inside a locked or closed payroll period.
exception_flows.handling: The locked day is not altered; an arrears item is raised for the next open run, payroll.input.stale and payroll.arrears.requested are emitted and payroll is notified.

exception_flows.condition: A recomputed day still contains an unpaired event.
exception_flows.handling: The day stays in EXCEPTION state and the exception remains in the queue for regularisation.

nfrs: Recomputes one month for 5,000 people in under 10 minutes.
Runs in an isolated worker and does not degrade interactive response times while running.
All derived reads pass the snapshot timestamp (valid_at, recorded_at), never the current time.

user_stories.want: a correction to a locked period to become arrears instead of changing the locked day
user_stories.so_that: a closed payroll always reconciles to the attendance it was paid on

acceptance.then: the 28 Aug attendance day is unchanged and an arrears item for E1018 is raised for the September run

acceptance.given: the same recompute
acceptance.then: payroll.input.stale has been emitted and I am notified of the arrears item with its reason

user_stories.so_that: a class change from mid-month does not rewrite the earlier days

acceptance.then: their response times stay within normal interactive targets

use_cases.name: View and export team attendance history
use_cases.goal: Give a manager a date-range history of attendance, leave, overtime, gate pass, late status and applied shift for their own team, on a phone, with a logged export.

stakeholders.interest: Only their own reporting manager can see their day-by-day history.
Exports of personal data are logged with who, what scope and when.
Supervisors answer their own team history questions without raising requests.

use_cases.trigger: A manager needs the history of a team member or the whole team for a date range.
preconditions: The manager holds an active reporting line to at least one person.
Attendance days for the range have been computed.
postconditions_success: Per-day history for the selected scope and range is shown, and any export is recorded with format, generator and scope (report.exported).
postconditions_failure: No data is returned for anyone outside the manager's reporting line at query time.

main_flow.action: Opens the team calendar, chooses a from and to date and selects one reportee or the whole team.
Returns per-day attendance status, leave, overtime, gate pass, late status and applied shift, scoped to the reporting line at query time.

steps: The platform returns one row per person per day for all current reportees.

exception_flows.condition: A request names a person outside the manager's reporting line, for example through an edited link.

exception_flows.condition: The phone is on a weak network.

use_cases.name: Log and approve project and task timesheets
use_cases.goal: Let knowledge workers record time against projects, tasks and cost centres, have it approved and pass approved cost to Finance.

stakeholders.interest: Approved time is costed to the right cost centre and project for allocation.
Reviews logged effort against attendance before approving.
Logs time quickly, starting from hours already known from attendance.

use_cases.trigger: A knowledge worker records the week's effort, usually at week end.
preconditions: The employee is assigned to at least one active project with tasks and a cost centre.
An approval chain for timesheets is defined for the employee's class and location (RL-010).
Attendance days for the week have been computed.
postconditions_success: An approved timesheet exists with lines per project, task, cost centre and day.
Costed lines are available to Finance for allocation and journal export to the ERP system.
postconditions_failure: A returned or rejected timesheet stays editable by the employee with the approver's comments, and nothing is costed.

main_flow.action: Opens the weekly timesheet, prefilled with each day's net attendance hours and the projects assigned to them.
Logs hours per day against project, task and cost centre, adding a short note per line.
Compares each day's logged hours with net attendance hours and flags days where logged time exceeds attendance.
Submits the week for approval.
Resolves the approval chain for the request type, class and location and routes the timesheet to the approver.
Approves the timesheet, or returns individual lines with a comment.
Costs each approved line at the cost-centre rate effective on the day and makes it available to Finance.
Reviews project cost allocation for the period and releases the allocation journal to the ERP system.

alternate_flows.condition: The approver returns some lines.
steps: Returned lines reopen for the employee with the comment; approved lines stay approved.
The employee corrects and resubmits only the returned lines.

alternate_flows.condition: The employee copies last week's project and task lines.
steps: Lines are copied with zero hours so only the hours need entering.

exception_flows.condition: Logged hours on a day exceed net attendance hours.
exception_flows.handling: Submission is blocked and the days are listed until hours are corrected or attendance is regularised.

exception_flows.condition: The costing period is already closed in Finance.
exception_flows.handling: Late-approved lines are costed into the next open period as adjustments and shown as such.

nfrs: A week with 10 lines can be entered and submitted on a phone in under 3 minutes.
Costing uses the rate effective on the worked date, not the approval date.

use_cases.name: Punch from mobile inside a geofence with a live selfie
use_cases.goal: Let field and remote workers punch from a phone only inside a configured geofence and with a liveness-checked selfie, keeping biometric templates on the device unless consented.

stakeholders.interest: Mobile punches are trustworthy and suspect ones are visible for review.
Biometric data is minimised and handled only with consent, in line with the DPDP Act 2023 (to be validated by Legal).
Can record attendance from a site or client location without a terminal.

use_cases.trigger: A field or remote worker opens the check-in screen on the mobile app.
preconditions: Mobile is an enabled punch source for the worker (RL-070) and at least one geofence is configured for the worker's location or assignment.
The worker has enrolled their face on the device; any consent to share the template is recorded.
The app has location permission.
postconditions_success: An attendance_event with source mobile, location and selfie reference is ingested through the standard punch path and the day is queued for derivation.
No biometric template has left the device unless a recorded consent allows it.
postconditions_failure: A punch outside the geofence or failing liveness is refused, and the attempt is visible to the time office.

main_flow.action: Opens the check-in screen on the mobile app.
Reads the device location and confirms it lies within a geofence configured for the worker's location or assignment.
Takes a selfie when prompted.
Runs the liveness check and face match on the device against the locally held template.
Confirms the punch direction, IN or OUT.
Records the punch with signed timestamp, geo_lat, geo_lng and selfie reference, sending only the match result, not the template.
Ingests the event through the standard punch path, de-duplicates it and queues the day for derivation.
Reviews refused or suspect mobile punches raised on the attendance exception queue.

alternate_flows.condition: The phone has no network.
steps: The punch is queued on the device with a signed timestamp, location and liveness result, and replayed on reconnect.

alternate_flows.condition: The worker has recorded consent for server-side matching.
steps: The template is transmitted under the consent record for server-side verification and the consent reference is stored with the event.

exception_flows.condition: The device location is outside every configured geofence.
exception_flows.handling: The punch is refused with the distance to the nearest geofence shown; the attempt is logged and the worker can seek regularisation.

exception_flows.condition: The liveness check fails.
exception_flows.handling: The worker may retry up to the tenant's configured limit; after that the punch is refused and an exception is raised for the time office.

exception_flows.condition: Location permission is denied on the phone.
exception_flows.handling: No punch can be recorded; the app explains that location is required for mobile attendance.

nfrs: Biometric templates never leave the device without a recorded consent.
The geofence and liveness checks complete within 3 seconds on a mid-range phone.
Queued offline mobile punches are retained for at least 7 days.

user_stories.so_that: my attendance is recorded without a terminal

acceptance.given: a worker who records consent
acceptance.then: the event stores the consent reference used for server-side matching

use_cases.name: Swap shifts and claim open shifts
use_cases.goal: Let workers swap shifts with colleagues or claim open shifts, subject to qualification, rest-period and overtime rules, with supervisor approval and an updated roster.

stakeholders.interest: Coverage changes stay within skills and statutory limits and are approved before they take effect.
The published roster matches what will be worked, reducing inferred-shift exceptions.
Can arrange cover for personal commitments without informal swaps.

use_cases.trigger: A worker requests a swap with a colleague or claims an open shift.
preconditions: A published roster exists for the period and open shifts, if any, are posted with required qualifications.
An approval chain for roster changes is defined (RL-010).
postconditions_success: The roster is republished with the swapped or claimed shifts and affected days are queued for recompute.
postconditions_failure: A swap or claim that breaks a rule is refused with the rule named and the roster is unchanged.

main_flow.action: Views their rostered shifts and the open shifts posted at their site.
Requests a swap of a named shift with a colleague, or claims an open shift.
For a swap, the named colleague accepts the exchange.
Checks qualifications, minimum rest between shifts, rest-day policy of the worker class and weekly overtime limits for both workers.
Routes the request to the supervisor through the approval chain resolved for type, class and location.
Approves or rejects the swap or claim.
Republishes the roster with the new assigned shifts and queues recompute for the affected dates.

alternate_flows.condition: Several workers claim the same open shift.
steps: All valid claims are shown to the supervisor in claim order with each claimant's weekly hours.
The supervisor picks one; the other claims are declined automatically.

alternate_flows.condition: The colleague declines the swap.

use_cases.name: Work flexi-time and manage a time bank
use_cases.goal: Support core-hours flexi-time with a time bank that records daily credits and debits and converts surplus to leave or overtime under policy.

stakeholders.interest: Balances long and short days within the rules and sees the balance at any time.
Core hours are covered and conversions are approved.
Conversions to overtime follow the same eligibility and approval path as ordinary overtime.

use_cases.trigger: A flexi-time worker's attendance day is computed, or the worker requests a conversion of banked time.
preconditions: A flexi policy with core hours, flexible band, daily target, bank cap and conversion rules applies to the worker's class.
The worker's attendance day has been computed (TIM-02).
postconditions_success: The day's surplus or deficit against target is posted to the time bank and the balance is visible to the worker.
An approved conversion is posted as leave credit or as an overtime record.
postconditions_failure: A conversion beyond the available balance or policy limit is refused and the bank is unchanged.

main_flow.action: Configures core hours, flexible band, daily target, bank cap and conversion ratios per worker class.
Punches in and out within the flexible band on a working day.
Checks presence across the whole core-hours window using the day's segments.
Posts the day's net minutes above or below the daily target to the time bank as a credit or debit.
Views the time-bank balance and its daily postings on My attendance.
Requests conversion of banked credit to leave or to overtime.
Approves or rejects the conversion.
Debits the bank and posts a leave credit or creates an overtime record for approval and payment.

alternate_flows.condition: The worker chooses conversion to overtime.
steps: The platform checks the worker's overtime eligibility before routing the request.

alternate_flows.condition: Posting a credit would take the balance above the bank cap.
steps: Only the amount up to the cap is credited; the excess is shown as not banked.

exception_flows.condition: The worker is absent for part of core hours.
exception_flows.handling: The day is flagged as a core-hours breach and treated as a late arrival or early departure under the disposition rules.

exception_flows.condition: The requested conversion exceeds the available balance.
exception_flows.handling: The request is refused and the available balance is shown.

exception_flows.condition: The worker's overtime eligibility is none.
exception_flows.handling: Conversion to overtime is refused; conversion to leave remains available.

nfrs: Every time-bank posting is traceable to the attendance day and ruleset version that produced it.
Flexi policy parameters are configuration per worker class, with no release needed to change them.

user_stories.want: my long and short days to balance in a time bank
user_stories.so_that: I can adjust my hours around commitments without penalty

acceptance.when: I work 09:00-18:30 on Monday with net 9h30m
acceptance.then: 90 minutes are credited to my time bank

acceptance.then: 60 minutes are debited and my balance shows 30 minutes

acceptance.given: a team member arrives at 09:50 and leaves at 16:05
acceptance.then: no breach is flagged

user_stories.so_that: surplus time becomes time off

acceptance.when: I request conversion and my manager approves
acceptance.then: one day of leave is credited and my bank balance becomes zero

acceptance.then: the request is refused and my available balance of 5h is shown

use_cases.name: Generate rosters from forecast labour demand
use_cases.goal: Generate a draft roster per line and site from forecast labour demand that honours skills, statutory limits, class rest days and worker preferences, then publish it after review.

stakeholders.interest: Each line has the required skills on every shift.
Rosters respect rest days and stated preferences where possible.
Generated rosters never plan work beyond statutory weekly limits (to be validated by Legal).

use_cases.trigger: The roster owner starts roster planning for the next period.
preconditions: A demand forecast of headcount by line, shift and skill exists for the period.
Worker skills, class rest-day policies, approved leave and preferences are recorded.
Shift definitions with non-overlapping inference windows exist for the site (RL-091).
postconditions_success: A published roster exists for the period, assigned shifts take effect and any already-worked dates affected are queued for recompute.
postconditions_failure: Where demand cannot be met within the rules, the shortfall is reported and no worker is planned beyond a limit.

main_flow.action: Loads or confirms the labour demand forecast by line, shift and skill for the roster period.
Reads available workers with skills, class rest-day policy, approved leave and stated preferences.
Generates a draft roster that fills demand within rest-day patterns and statutory weekly limits, favouring stated preferences.
Shows coverage per line and shift, unfilled demand, projected overtime and rule warnings for the draft.
Adjusts individual assignments, with rules rechecked on each change.
Reviews coverage for their lines and confirms or comments.
Publishes the roster so its shifts become the assigned shifts for the period.
Queues recompute for any affected dates already worked and notifies workers of their shifts.

alternate_flows.condition: The supervisor requests changes.
steps: Comments return to the roster owner, who adjusts the draft.

alternate_flows.condition: No forecast is available for a line.
steps: The roster owner copies the previous period's demand for that line as the forecast.

exception_flows.condition: Demand cannot be met without breaching a weekly limit or a rest day.
exception_flows.handling: The draft leaves the demand unfilled and reports the shortfall by line and shift; no worker is planned beyond the limit.

exception_flows.condition: A manual change places a worker on their class's rest day.
exception_flows.handling: The change is allowed only with a warning naming the rest-day rule, which is recorded on the assignment.

nfrs: A draft roster for one site of 1,000 workers over 4 weeks is generated in under 2 minutes.
Every generated assignment can show the demand line and rule checks that justified it.
